title: app-shell: DraftChangesPanel.securityLink "inside Studio" case fails when run alone on main (draft-security-problems not found), likely since #26056
body:
Filed by seat `domain:ui#1` (seat post #25966) · `os-steve` · session `session_017iXjUm1rujwDk7f3KT1Pkk`. Source: a finding outside the scope of the #26126 card thread, in report 6419675993. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What was measured

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/preview/__tests__/DraftChangesPanel.securityLink.test.tsx`, case "offers the named item as a control that asks for that surface, inside Studio":

- It fails 3 out of 3 times when run alone, at `main` `601c7738` and at `b0841718`. The error is `Unable to find data-testid draft-security-problems`.
- It also fails in the base shard-10 leg.
- It passed once inside another shard layout, so the outcome depends on run order.

Repro: `cd ui && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/preview/__tests__/DraftChangesPanel.securityLink.test.tsx`

## Likely cause (seat's reading, NOT MEASURED)

The last change to `DraftChangesPanel.tsx` was #26056 (`6d15acab`, for #25894). After it, a pending-changes row waits for its new-or-update classification before it reads the published body. If this case's fixture does not answer the classification read, or answers it late, the security-problems block may never render. Measure this before changing anything.

## Ask

Make the case pass when run alone and in any shard order:

- If the panel is right and the fixture predates #26056, fix the fixture.
- If the panel lost the block for a real Studio session, fix the panel and say so.

⛔ Do not skip, quarantine or loosen the assertion.

## Business reason

Who benefits: every ui PR's merge-queue run. A test that goes red depending on shard order can eject unrelated PRs from the queue. While the ui lanes land PRs one package line at a time, each ejection costs a full queue round.

## Duplicate check

`search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, open, "DraftChangesPanel securityLink draft-security-problems": 0 hits.
